retrieval.injection_point_format: before ## Task, _format_retrieved_block -- byte-identical function reused from build_probe_prompts.py
retrieval.base_prompt: byte-identical reuse of data/parsed/prompts_main/<case_id>__baseline.json -- NOT reconstructed from beta_parsed/alpha, so base prompt is guaranteed identical to the k=3 run's base prompt
retrieval.probe_G_k_ablation: deterministic top-k by (statute_section, statute_subsection, limitation-pattern Jaccard) score, same _g_score() as frozen G. VALIDATED NESTED vs k=3: G1's single pick == frozen G(k=3)'s top-1 pick for all 100 cases (0 mismatches); G5's first 3 picks == frozen G(k=3)'s all 3 picks for all 100 cases (0 mismatches). G's ranking does not depend on k, so this nesting is structural, not incidental.
retrieval.probe_F_k_ablation: uniform random via random.Random(sha256(case_id+'::F')[:8]).sample(pool, k=k) -- SAME seed tag as frozen k=3 F, for reproducibility. CAVEAT (documented, not a hidden default): Python's random.sample() does not guarantee that the k=1 draw is a prefix of the k=3 draw or that k=5 is a superset of it -- sample() takes different internal code paths depending on k relative to len(pool). F1/F3/F5 for a given case are same-seeded but NOT guaranteed-nested random subsets of the 4,221-entry pool.
retrieval.validation: checked all 400 rendered files (100 cases x {F1,F5,G1,G5}): 0 self-retrievals, 0 duplicate-app_num-within-a-case's-picks, retrieved-count exactly matches requested k in every file.

prompt_size.method: mean user_chars, measured directly on rendered prompts (not estimated)
prompt_size.note: k=1 prompts run ~15% smaller than k=3, k=5 prompts ~15% larger, roughly linear in number of injected exemplars (~1.5-1.8k chars/exemplar) -- used below for cost projection.

generation.seed_caveat: No true LLM sampling seed is passed to any provider in this codebase's run_main.py -- same caveat as the main run and dense-G. Temperature=0.3 + 3 reps is the design's actual answer to stochasticity.
generation.parse_failure_policy: unchanged from main run / dense-G: call_with_retry retries on 429/5xx up to max_retries=4 with backoff, hard-fails immediately on 400/401/403/404; failures logged to outputs/<model>_kablation/_failures.jsonl, resumable via --skip-failed.
generation.baseline_and_k3_reuse: baseline and k=3 (F,G) NOT regenerated -- existing scored tables reused as-is (see scope.k3_source above). Only F1, F5, G1, G5 are new generation.

cost_projection_usd.method: historical real per-call $/call from the k=3 Probe G run (dense_G_run_config.json), scaled by the measured prompt_size char-ratio for each k (input-token-dominated approximation -- output length is roughly k-independent, so this likely mildly overstates the swing at k=1 and k=5; not an observed number, will be replaced by real cost_usd once generation runs, same as the dense-G precedent).
cost_projection_usd.comparable_reference: dense-G's own 1,200-call run projected at $18.74, actual real cost came in at $18.32 -- i.e. this style of projection has historically landed within ~2% of real spend on this exact harness.

scoring_plan_once_generated.pipeline: same deterministic scorers as k=3/dense-G: compute_c1.py score (lexical), compute_c1_embedding.py (semantic, all-MiniLM-L6-v2), compute_c2.py score, compute_c3.py score, compute_c5.py score -- pointed at outputs/<model>_kablation/ for all 4 models at once via --roots.

stats_plan.script: scripts/wilcoxon_kablation.py -- adapted from wilcoxon_denseG.py, same method: per-case mean of 3 reps, paired Wilcoxon signed-rank (baseline vs probe) two-sided, bootstrap 95% CI on median diff (10k resamples, seed 42), Holm-Bonferroni within the family of NEW tests only (F1,F5,G1,G5 x 4 metrics x 4 models = 64 tests), consistent with how dense-G's H family (16 tests) was corrected separately from the frozen F/G-at-k3 tests.
stats_plan.k3_baseline_note: F(k=3) and G(k=3) vs baseline p-values are reported alongside for context (same as dense-G's table showed baseline->F and baseline->G p next to baseline->H p) but are NOT part of the new-test Holm family -- they are the pre-existing main-run comparisons.
stats_plan.headline_focus: C5 (H1/prior-injection) and C2 (revision locality) called out per the request; full 64-test table (C1 lexical, C1 semantic, C2, C3, C5 x F1/F5/G1/G5 x 4 models) also produced.
stats_plan.NOT_YET_RUN: requires F1/F5/G1/G5 generation + scoring, which is blocked -- see BLOCKERS. Script is written and tested to fail loudly (exit 1, list missing files) rather than fabricate numbers if the score tables don't exist, same discipline as wilcoxon_denseG.py.
